Article Title: Rudraprayag district launches ‘Donate One Book, Plant a Tree of Knowledge’ drive
Article Text: NEW DELHI: The Rudraprayag district administration on Saturday launched the “Donate One Book, Plant a Tree of Knowledge” campaign under the Harela initiative, with district magistrate Vishal Mishra inaugurating the drive by donating a book and calling on residents to contribute to building a shared repository of knowledge.Speaking at the launch, Mishra said that just as people plant trees and renew their commitment to nature during the Harela festival, donating books can help spread knowledge across the community.He said a single good book can change an individual's life and serve as a source of inspiration and guidance for future generations, urging every resident to donate at least one book of their choice to help build a lasting repository of knowledge for the district.According to the district administration, the donated books will be made available to students, youth, aspirants preparing for competitive examinations and the general public.Highlighting the enduring value of books, Mishra said they retain their relevance across generations by carrying knowledge, values, experience and ideas that continue to guide society.He said the campaign aims not only to collect books but also to cultivate a reading culture, encourage knowledge sharing and provide constructive direction to young people.Appealing for wider participation, the district magistrate urged departmental officers and staff, elected representatives, teachers, social organisations, NGOs and citizens to actively support the initiative.He asked every individual to contribute at least one useful and inspirational book, saying that even a small donation can significantly impact a needy student’s future.Expressing confidence in the campaign, Mishra said collective community participation would help transform the initiative into a wider movement while reinforcing the importance of knowledge across the district.Chief development officer Rajendra Singh Rawat, additional district magistrate Shyam Singh Rana, district development officer Manvinder Kaur, chief medical officer Ram Prakash, district finance and statistics officer Sandeep Bhatt, chief agriculture officer Lokendra Bisht, district supply officer KS Kohli, district social welfare officer TR Maletha, sub-divisional magistrate (Ukhimath) Anil Rawat, along with officers and staff from various departments, were present at the launch.
Article Summary: The Rudraprayag district administration on Saturday launched the “Donate One Book, Plant a Tree of Knowledge’ campaign under the Harela initiative. District magistrate Vishal Mishra inaugurated the drive by donating a book and calling on residents to contribute to building a shared repository of knowledge.

Article Title: SC: Will go the extra mile to fix issues, make NEET foolproof
Article Text:
SC assures Neet will be foolproof

NEW DELHI: Amid street protests by the youth against paper leaks and demands that govt fix accountability and bring reforms, the Supreme Court Friday said the system's ad hocism was "troubling", which could not be allowed to go on and assured that it would "tread an extra mile" to fix the problems and make NEET foolproof.With solicitor general Tushar Mehta contending that govt was ready to tread "10 extra miles" to protect the interests of students and that the matter was being supervised at the highest level, a bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe asked him to expeditiously take a decision. It granted time till Aug 3 to brief them about the contours of the new system.The court also sought the Centre's response on implementing computer-based test for medical entrance on the lines of IIT-JEE. The court was hearing a batch of petitions, including ones filed by the Federation of All India Medical Association and United Doctors Front, seeking the court's intervention to make NEET tamper-free. The SG, at the outset of the hearing, said the issue was under serious consideration of govt and sought adjournment for a few days. He said some developments were likely to take place soon.The bench, however, pointed out various issues which govt needed to address, including implementation of recommendations of the high-level committee headed by former Isro chairman K Radhakrishnan."We will highlight a couple of things we wanted to indicate... Last time, you mentioned the Radhakrishnan committee's recommendations. There is a specific reference to the governing board. So your affidavit should indicate what has been done with respect to the governing board, which would consist of transparency, nominations and stakeholders," the bench said.SC said it will keep monitoring the process till the system is institutionalised. "We are focusing on institutionalisation. Ad-hocism has troubled us the most throughout these years.""A very important aspect is the transition to computer-based testing.... Can it be shifted? How will the data be transferred? How will the data be protected? Data safety is the most important aspect. You indicate to us. Cybersecurity, who is to undertake it, how it is to be conducted etc," the bench asked.Dr Radhakrishnan, head of the monitoring committee constituted by SC in 2024 to suggest ways to strengthen NEET, earlier informed the court the committee had submitted 35 long-term recommendations and around 60 short-term recommendations, most of which had already been implemented. He said the reforms had largely yielded positive results in NEET-PG 2025, which was conducted "mostly satisfactorily" except for some issues such as power outages.
Article Summary: Supreme Court says system's ad hocism was "troubling", which could not be allowed to go on. Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe granted time till Aug 3 to brief them about the contours of the new system.

Article Title: Why the world is coming to India for medical treatment — and not just because it is cheaper
Article Text:
People coming from various countries to India for cardio surgeries, IVF treatment, dental care, etc.

What is medical tourism?

Government focus

India ranks 10th on medical tourism index

Why patients are choosing India

Beyond affordability

Areas for improvement

The next phase of growth

A hip replacement in Vadodara. A dental procedure in Chennai. An IVF treatment in Delhi. Every year, hundreds of thousands of patients travel to India not for its monuments or beaches, but for its medical care.What was once driven largely by patients from neighbouring countries seeking affordable treatment has evolved into a broader medical travel ecosystem.Industry estimates cited by the Economic Survey 2025–26 and the government project India's medical tourism market to grow from around $8.7 billion in 2025 to $16.2 billion by 2030. Over the same period, the global Medical Value Travel market is projected to expand from $115.6 billion in 2022 to $286.1 billion by 2030. Additionally, India's broader hospital and healthcare delivery market is expected to grow at 10–12 per cent annually, reaching nearly Rs 12 trillion by FY30, with private hospital chains projected to expand capacity from around 70,000 beds to more than 108,000 by 2030.India ranks 10th among the world's 46 medical tourism destinations, according to the Medical Tourism Index 2020–21.Let’s dive deep into the medical world and see how much potential India offers to tourists.Medical tourism refers to patients travelling outside their home country to seek planned medical treatment. While lower treatment costs remain a major factor, patients also consider waiting times, access to specialists, quality of care, language support and post-treatment follow-up when choosing a destinationFor India, the demand spans a wide range of services, from cardiac surgery and joint replacements to cancer treatment, fertility care, organ transplants, dental treatment, cosmetic procedures and neurological interventions.Improvements in digital consultations and easier access to treatment information have also made it simpler for patients to compare hospitals and plan their care before travelling.The Union Budget 2026–27 has proposed the development of five Regional Medical Hubs in partnership with state governments and the private sector. These hubs will combine medical, educational and research facilities, along with AYUSH centres and dedicated Medical Value Tourism facilitation centres.To further facilitate such travel, India offers e-Medical Visa and e-Medical Attendant Visa facilities, which have been extended to nationals of 172 countries, along with newer e-AYUSH Visa categories for those seeking traditional Indian systems of medicine. The government is also upgrading its Heal in India (Medical Value Travel) portal into a single platform for hospital discovery, treatment planning, bookings, payments and post-operative care, while airport concierge services have been proposed to assist international patients on arrival.Notably, according to government data, India has 69,364 hospitals; including 43,486 private and 25,778 public facilities, along with around 1.2 million registered doctors and more than 1,299 NABH-accredited hospitals as of 2026. Several hospitals are also accredited by the Joint Commission International (JCI), with most located in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai and Hyderabad.For patients who make the journey, affordability is often only part of the story.India recorded 507,244 foreign arrivals for medical treatment in 2025, accounting for about 5.5 per cent of total foreign tourist arrivals that year; as compared to about 112,000 in 2009. Bangladesh was the largest source market with 3,25,127 arrivals, followed by Iraq (30,989), Uzbekistan (13,699), Somalia (11,506), Turkmenistan (10,231), Oman (9,738) and Kenya (9,357).People have given various reasons for choosing India.American traveller Charlie Evans, who sought treatment for seasonal flu and an ear complaint at a hospital in Rishikesh, said he was initially hesitant about seeking medical care in a foreign country. However, he described being greeted by English-speaking staff, facing almost no waiting time and receiving treatment using equipment comparable to what he had seen in the United States.Evans said his consultation, medication and treatment cost around $10–20, compared with an estimated $150 for a similar visit in the US. "I got better care in Rishikesh, faster and cheaper, than I've ever gotten at home," he said.Beyond the lower cost, Evans said what stood out was the professionalism of the medical staff. "The doctor who treated me could have easily been practising in the US," he said, adding that healthcare in India felt to him less like a profit-driven system and more focused on patient care.The experience reflects a broader trend, where patients increasingly weigh convenience and quality alongside costs.American content creator Kristen Fischer, who lives in India, has also praised the country's healthcare system. While she believes the US offers a better overall hospital experience, she said she prefers India's healthcare system because it is "simple, affordable, fast" and offers "quality treatment.""One thing I love about Indian healthcare is that you pay before treatment. Then after you leave the hospital you never have to pay or worry about anything else again," Fischer said, contrasting it with the US, where patients can receive bills "for months after" treatment. She also argued that India's upfront pricing makes costs more transparent, unlike in the US where insurance often shields patients from the true cost of treatment, contributing to higher healthcare expenses."The cost is clearly defined before treatment. This allows people to shop around for a good deal according to their budget," she said.Fischer, in her series of social media posts, has also highlighted the accessibility of healthcare in India, saying patients can often see a doctor the same day without an appointment, unlike in the US where consultations can take weeks. She has described Indian doctors as "way less rushed and more attentive to your needs" and recounted receiving treatment for a thumb injury at a Delhi hospital in about 45 minutes for just Rs 50.The cost advantage is evident even for routine procedures too. Sej, who lives in Utrecht in the Netherlands, said she schedules her dental appointments around her trips to India. "A 30-minute teeth cleaning costs around 185 euros near where I live. In Lucknow, I pay about Rs 3,000 for the same treatment," she said.Aditya Oza, CEO of CureMeAbroad, which connects international patients with accredited hospitals, said India is beginning to attract patients who once favoured destinations such as Turkey and Thailand.He cited a case where two people who had earlier travelled to Turkey for treatment but chose India for their latest procedure. "Patients who've already been through this once, who know what to look for, are increasingly landing on India specifically. The accreditation is there, the specialist experience is there, and the cost gap is often the widest of any destination," he said."What's changed is that patients now have a way to verify all of that upfront instead of guessing."Hospital executives believe India's competitiveness will increasingly depend on the overall patient experience rather than just costs.Dr Sonia Lal Gupta, joint managing director of Metro Group of Hospitals, said accreditation, transparent clinical outcomes and accountability remain important differentiators."What we haven't fully built yet is the trust and the experience around that care, and that is where the real opportunity lies," she said.She added that support should extend beyond the hospital stay, covering everything from the first enquiry and medical visa assistance to treatment, recovery and follow-up consultations after patients return home.Meanwhile, Dr Sharan Shivaraj Patil, founder and chairman of SPARSH Group of Hospitals, said providers are investing in dedicated international patient services to make treatment easier from the first inquiry through recovery. It includes pre-arrival teleconsultations, medical visa assistance, transparent treatment plans with cost estimates, airport transfers, accommodation support, language interpretation, culturally appropriate meals and post-treatment follow-up. "As the expectations of international patients continue to evolve, the focus remains on delivering world-class clinical outcomes complemented by personalised, culturally sensitive and compassionate care," he added.Meanwhile, UK content creator Reuben Charles, who is currently in Guwahati, said he was impressed by the convenience and professionalism of his healthcare experience in India after using an at-home medical service to get some blood tests. He said the healthcare professional who attended to him was knowledgeable, spoke fluent English and took the time to explain the procedure in detail."The service was great. It was very, very quick as well. It came right to my house," Charles said.He believes India's combination of quality, accessibility and convenience makes it an attractive destination for medical tourism, particularly for international patients who can afford private healthcareBritish traveller Jenny Mowbray, who spent five months in Kochi, also said India's healthcare system stood out for its speed, affordability and flexibility. Unable to easily access a second neurological opinion through the UK's public health system, she chose to undergo consultations and diagnostic tests in India."For me, the biggest attraction is the combination of accessibility, speed, quality, cost and choice," she said, highlighting the specialists' consult within a day, complete MRI scans and blood tests almost immediately and receiving results within hours.While describing her overall experience as "efficient, patient-centred and highly accessible," Mowbray said better access to verified information on hospitals, specialties and treatment costs could make India's medical tourism ecosystem even more attractive for international patients.Recounting her experience she said, " Before coming to India, I had already used healthcare services in Malaysia, Sri Lanka and Tunisia for a range of issues including my neurological concerns, gynaecological care and knee cartilage damage. During my five-month stay in Kochi, I wanted to have a mole checked and also revisit my neurological symptoms for peace of mind. "I was able to make appointments with both a dermatologist and a neurologist for the very next day.The dermatology consultation was extremely thorough," she added.Sharing another perspective, Jai Prakash, founder of Health Voyage Global, a medical tourism consultancy, said patients often come to India after struggling to get the right diagnosis. "Many patients believe they can receive the right diagnosis and treatment in India at a fraction of the cost they would pay elsewhere," he said. "Indian doctors are exposed to advanced medical equipment and global treatment protocols, allowing them to offer high-quality care with shorter treatment timelines and lower overall costs,” he added.Not every patient travels to India purely for lower costs or better hospitals. For some, crossing borders also offers privacy. A Delhi resident recounted how her neighbour had travelled alone to India from Nepal for IVF treatment because she faced social stigma and family pressure back home over fertility issues. Seeking treatment away from her community allowed her to undergo the procedure without the scrutiny and judgement.Despite rising patient numbers, hospitals say access to care remains uneven across the country.Dr Bharat S Mody, chairman of Welcare Hospital in Vadodara, said India attracts a steady stream of patients from neighbouring countries such as Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Afghanistan, as well as from Africa and parts of Central Asia. However, he believes the country has yet to realise its full potential in attracting patients from Europe, the US and other developed markets.Mody said international patients are drawn by India's competitive pricing and medical expertise, but most treatment remains concentrated in metro cities, even though tier-2 centres can offer comparable quality at lower costs.Apart from this, he emphasised the medical visa process remains another hurdle for overseas patients."Our experience has also been that the government portal which issues the medical visa is not user-friendly," he said, adding that it "frustrates a potential patient wanting to come to India for medical treatment."He cited the example of Marco Bellaro, an Italian living in Indonesia, who travelled to Vadodara for a total hip replacement after finding the hospital online. Although Bellaro initially had concerns about hygiene standards and hospital infrastructure, Mody said those were addressed during consultations. The surgery was successful, but the medical visa process proved cumbersome, reiterating that simpler visa procedures and stronger global branding could help India attract more overseas patientsDr Alok Khullar, Group CEO of RJ Corp Healthcare, also emphasised on simplifying medical visa procedures, increasing the number of internationally accredited hospitals, improving coordination between airports and hospitals, and expanding multilingual support remain key priorities."Greater transparency around treatment costs and clinical outcomes will further strengthen confidence among patients and their families," he said.Patients, too, gave suggestions to fill out gaps beyond treatment itself. Charlie Evans, the American traveller, said a dedicated website or app for international patients, featuring hospital rankings, verified patient reviews and guidance on where to seek treatment for specific conditions, would make it easier for foreigners to navigate India's healthcare system with confidence.Adarsh Yadav, founder of healthcare companion platform CARESY, also emphasised on holistic services and care, saying India already has the clinical expertise to compete globally but must also focus on the patient journey. "If we can combine this with a smoother and more reassuring patient experience, India can become an even stronger destination for medical travellers," he said.India already has the ingredients - a large healthcare network, skilled medical professionals and a growing international patient base. As demand for cross-border healthcare grows globally, industry stakeholders believe India has the potential to attract even more.However, realising that opportunity, will require more than competitive treatment costs. The next phase of growth will depend on how effectively hospitals, governments, airlines, hotels, insurers and digital platforms work together to create a seamless patient journey.
Article Summary: India ranks 10th among the world's 46 medical tourism destinations, according to the Medical Tourism Index 2020–21. India recorded 507,244 foreign arrivals for medical treatment in 2025, accounting for about 5.5 per cent of total foreign tourist arrivals. Bangladesh was the largest source market with 3,25,127 arrivals.

Article Title: Fast-track courts in slow lane now, backlog 2.5 lakh cases
Article Text:
Massive backlog in fast-track courts

Justice delayed

NEW DELHI: Fast-track special courts, which are meant to complete trials within a year of taking cognisance of offences related to rape and Pocso Act , have not been working at the expected speed. In 2025, which saw more than 1.4 lakh rape and Pocso cases being registered, only 66,500 were disposed of.The backlog of cases had reached 2.5 lakh on Dec 31, 2025. The trend has been similar over the last three years, with the total pendency at over 2 lakh. Since fast-track special courts were constituted in 2019, case pendency has always been around 2 lakh over the last seven years despite the scheme mandating time-bound trials."The scheme has been extended twice, with the last extension valid up to March 31, 2026, for establishment of 790 fast-track special courts. The scheme has now been extended up to Sept 30 this year," law minister Arjun Ram Meghwal informed Parliament in a written response Thursday.The minister added that according to information made available by high courts, 775 fast-track special courts, including 398 exclusive Pocso (e-Pocso) courts, were functional in 29 states/Union Territories as of April.Centre and states share expenditure on these courts in a 60:40 ratio.This covers the salaries of one judicial officer along with seven support staff for each fast-track court, in addition to a grant for meeting day-to-day expenses.Since the inception of the scheme, Centre has released Rs 1,260 crore to states and UTs to ensure the courts functioned smoothly, Meghwal said.The minister said he had written to chief ministers and Chief Justices of high courts regarding the "need for timely action and strict compliance with timelines under Pocso Act and BNSS".Meghwal, however, said it was the responsibility of states and HCs to recruit judges and fill vacant positions of judicial officers in district and subordinate courts, including fast-track ones.
Article Summary: In 2025, which saw more than 1.4 lakh rape and Pocso cases being registered, only 66,500 were disposed of. The trend has been similar over the last three years, with the total pendency at over 2 lakh. Since the inception of the scheme, Centre has released Rs 1,260 crore to states and UTs to ensure the courts functioned smoothly.

Article Title: SC bans posting court clips on social media
Article Text:
Apex court said any online use of audiovisual excerpts from hearings must have the approval of SC or HC.

Lawyers misusing court clips to lure clients, SC told

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Friday barred the uploading, sharing and circulation of video clips from live-streamed court proceedings on social media and digital platforms, after finding that edited clips with biased commentary were flooding social media. Apex court said any online use of audiovisual excerpts from hearings must have the approval of SC or HC.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana passed the interim order after senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for journalist PIL petitioner Harshita Grover, said some of these clips circulating on social media are edited with a devious mind and that a mischievous narrative is superimposed to project a negative image of the judiciary.Backing the PIL and a regulatory mechanism, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said use of AI has led to a manifold rise in spread of motivated narratives on social media, and could become a tool to malign judiciary's image.SC sought responses from govt, HCs and social media platforms - YouTube, X, WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram - in two weeks."As an interim measure, no excerpts from live-streamed judicial proceedings will be posted, transmitted, stored, hosted or circulated on any social media or digital platforms without prior permission of SC secretary general or registrars general of jurisdictional HCs," the bench said.Senior advocate Vikas Singh, who is also president of Supreme Court Bar Association, flagged advocates posting clips of court proceedings involving them on social media apparently to boost popularity and attract clients.SC has sought a response from Bar Council of India as Advocates Act bars lawyers from advertising or soliciting clients directly or indirectly.Apart from social media activity, many law firms now have engaged PR professionals who approach journalists to incorporate quotes from them in news articles.The misuse of court clips on social media was such that the CJI-led bench considered suspending the live streaming of judicial hearings, which began during the Covid lockdown."If the digital data generated from the court hearings after going public becomes difficult to regulate, we will consider restricting live-streaming of court proceedings, as we do not want it to become a 24x7 entertainment channel. It is trivialising the judiciary," the bench said.When the bench said availability of links to live proceedings could be restricted only to advocates and litigants on demand, Singh said live streaming should not be stopped as it gives transparency to judicial proceedings.The petitioner said fair reporting of judicial proceedings was protected under the right to free speech under Article 19, and the protection did not extend to mischievous and denigrating contents that interfere with the administration of justice, spread misinformation or subject judicial institutions to organised vilification campaigns."Misleading thumbnails, clickbait headlines, provocative commentary, and edited courtroom clips encourage sensationalism rather than accurate reporting. These practices distort public understanding of judicial proceedings and erode confidence in the justice delivery system," Harshita Grover said.
Article Summary: Apex court said any online use of audiovisual excerpts from hearings must have the approval of SC or HC. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said use of AI has led to a rise in spread of motivated narratives on social media.

Article Title: 4.1cr kids obese, ICMR seeks tighter curbs
Article Text:
Nearly 4.1 crore Indian children are already overweight or obese

NEW DELHI: With World Obesity Atlas 2026 saying nearly 4.1 crore Indian children are already overweight or obese, Indian Council of Medical Research unveiled a roadmap this week to halt the trend.Key proposals include front-of-pack nutrition labelling, restrictions on market-ing of unhealthy foods to chi-ldren, healthier school food environments, improved nutrition literacy, and fiscal measures such as taxes on foods high in fat, salt and sugar (HFSS).It also calls for stricter enforcement of existing FSSAI regulations that prohibit sale and advertising of foods high in saturated fat, trans fat, added sugar and sodium within school campuses and within 50m of their gates. The document recommends routine inspections, stronger monitoring and greater accountability to improve compliance.A pilot assessment in UP private schools found ultra-processed snacks and sugary drinks were widely available in school canteens, nutrition services were limited, and existing nutrition policies were poorly implemented. The report says the absence of a legally operational definition of HFSS foods has weakened enforcement of regulations.The report warns India could account for more than 11% of the global childhood obesity burden by 2030 if current trends continue. It also estimates that unhealthy diets account for 56.4% of the country's disease burden, with easy access to HFSS foods, aggressive marketing and poor nutrition literacy driving obesity.The roadmap, launched by Niti Aayog member (health) M Srinivas under the ICMR-NIN-led 'Let's Fix Our Food' initiative, brings together 10 policy briefs developed over nearly three years of research.
Article Summary: World Obesity Atlas 2026 says nearly 4.1 crore Indian children are already overweight or obese. Indian Council of Medical Research unveiled a roadmap this week to halt the trend. Key proposals include front-of-pack nutrition labelling, restrictions on market-ing of unhealthy foods.

Article Title: Bill moots 10 years in prison, fine of Rs 10 crore for paper leaks
Article Text:
People participate in a protest against the alleged NEET-UG paper leak

NEW DELHI: In a major crackdown on examination malpractices and paper leak mafia, Cabinet on Friday approved a draft bill proposing up to 10 years in jail and a maximum fine of Rs 10 crore for those involved in such crimes. The Cabinet chaired by PM Modi also approved statutory backing for fast-track courts for trials of such cases and to dispose of them "within three months".The decision came barely hours after Modi, in a message on social media, vowed the strictest measures to prevent paper leaks, which have a devastating effect on the country's youth. PM has said that the proposed amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 will be introduced in Parliament and efforts will be made for faster passage.TOI has learned that the bill will ensure time-bound completion of investigation. A senior govt functionary said the 2024 law has "helped a lot" and several gangs have been busted and actions have been taken in the past two years. Govt aims to strengthen this and address any shortcomings to protect the interest of youth, he added.People aware of the development said the jail term for individuals resorting to unfair means and offences under the proposed law would be at least five years as against the current provision of minimum three years' in prison.The jail term could be up to 10 years. They added that fines for such offenders would also be increased, though they didn't specify the amount. At present, the fine is capped at Rs 10 lakh for individual offenders.Officials said that in case of organised crimes by a person or group of people, including the examination authority or service provider, the jail term would be 10 years with Rs 10 crore fine. At present, the fine for such organised crime is Rs 1 crore.The proposed law is also likely to bring coaching centres under its purview for any malpractices by them.The existing law is aimed at curbing leaks, unfair means as well as organised malpractices in recruitment examinations like Union Public Service Commission, SSC, and entrance tests such as NEET, JEE, and CUET.
Article Summary: Draft bill proposes up to 10 years in jail and a maximum fine of Rs 10 crore for those involved in such crimes. Cabinet also approved statutory backing for fast- track courts for trials of such cases and to dispose of them "within three months" Decision came barely hours after PM Modi vowed the strictest measures to prevent paper leaks.

Article Title: Ladakh outfit welcomes end of Wangchuk's fast
Article Text:
Gelek Phunchok, convenor LAB, in a statement said “the LAB welcomes Sonam Wangchuk’s decision to end his fast, a step it had consistently requested in view of his deteriorating health.”

SRINAGAR: Representatives of the Leh Apex Body (LAB), who were present at Gurugram ’s Medanta Hospital when climate activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike Thursday night, have welcomed his decision.“We had earlier urged him to end his hunger strike. We wanted to see him alive. We were deeply concerned about his deteriorating health, and we are relieved he has ended his hunger strike,” LAB co-chairman Chering Dorjay Lakrook said.He said he and his three other LAB representatives were there at Medanta when Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh arrived and Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike in their presence.Gelek Phunchok, convener of LAB, said a delegation led by Lakrook had travelled to New Delhi to meet Wangchuk but was made to wait for several days before permission to meet him was granted.Wangchuk too is a member of the LAB.Early this month, the LAB appealed to Wangchuk to end his hunger strike and return to Ladakh, saying his presence was needed as negotiations with the Centre had reached a critical stage.On May 22 this year, Wangchuk was part of the Ladakhi delegation that held talks with the MHA subcommittee over their demands for the region.However, on July 3, Wangchuk couldn’t participate in the talks held between the Ladakhi leaders and the MHA as he was on hunger strike at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi.
Article Summary: Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike at Gurugram’s Medanta Hospital Thursday night. Representatives of the Leh Apex Body (LAB), who were present at the hospital, welcomed his decision. LAB appealed to Wangchuk to end his hunger strike and return to Ladakh.

Article Title: Haryana’s air pollution action plan: Centre suggests strict enforcement and accelerated implementation to curb pollution in a time-bound manner
Article Text:
Centre reviewed measures taken by the Haryana govt to address the issue of air pollution

NEW DELHI: The Centre on Friday reviewed measures taken by the Haryana govt to address the issue of air pollution in Delhi-NCR, and emphasised the need for “accelerated implementation, stronger inter-agency coordination and strict enforcement” to ensure substantial reduction in pollution before the onset of the winter season when stubble burning and meteorological conditions raise the levels of pollutants.The meeting, chaired by Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav in Gurugram, held extensive discussions on Haryana’s air pollution action plan and multiple steps, which are being taken, with particular focus on legacy waste, road dust, industrial pollution and strengthening the infrastructure to enable accelerated EV adoption.Haryana chief minister Nayab Singh Saini and senior officials of the state govt attended the meeting."The window before the winter season must be fully utilized to implement pollution control measures in mission mode. Timely execution, effective coordination and strict enforcement will be critical to achieving visible improvements in Delhi-NCR's air quality,” said Yadav while emphasising the urgency of timely action.On critical issue of stubble burning that increases level of air pollutants in Delhi-NCR during every winter, Yadav urged the state govt to bridge gaps in procurement of Crop Residue Management (CRM) machinery and accelerate establishment of Custom Hiring Centres.He also emphasised the need for intensive Information, Education and Communication (IEC) campaigns and farmer training programmes to promote effective use of CRM equipment. He suggested that local elected representatives identify stubble-burning hotspots in coordination with Gram Panchayats, and asked District Collectors to survey industrial units and document their crop residue storage and consumption capacities to facilitate efficient demand-supply management.“The state authorities were also advised to ensure adequate availability of crop residue balers,” said a statement from the environment ministry on the review meeting.It said, “The minister also reviewed progress on construction and demolition waste management and requested that the establishment of Secondary Collection Centres for C&D waste be expedited. He also stressed that liquidation of legacy waste should be undertaken on a war footing.”Referring to municipal solid waste (MSW) and biomass burning, Yadav called for the constitution of dedicated task forces and emphasized achieving 100% collection of municipal solid waste and biomass to eliminate littering and prevent open burning.On the issue of End-of-Life (EoL) vehicles, Yadav requested the authorities to expedite issuance of No Objection Certificates (NOCs) for transfer of eligible EoL vehicles outside the NCR, while simultaneously encouraging scientific scrapping of old and unfit vehicles. He also called for faster replacement of old polluting vehicles with electric vehicles under the ‘Parivartan’ scheme.“The minister requested that Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras be installed at all fuel stations for effective implementation of the ‘No PUCC, No Fuel’ initiative. Stressing the need to improve urban traffic management, Yadav asked the authorities to identify traffic congestion hotspots on a mission mode and implement suitable mitigation measures at the earliest,” said the official statement.Reviewing industrial pollution control measures, Yadav stressed the need for accelerated installation of Online Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (OCEMS) and Air Pollution Control Devices (APCDs) across industrial units.
Article Summary: The Centre on Friday reviewed measures taken by the Haryana govt to address the issue of air pollution in Delhi-NCR. The meeting, chaired by Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav in Gurugram, held extensive discussions on air pollution action plan.

Article Title: Fast-track special courts slow as backlog mounts; nearly 2.5 lakh cases pending
Article Text:
Fast-track special courts slow as backlog mounts; nearly 2.5 lakh cases pending

BENGALURU: At a time when Centre has announced setting up of Fast-Track Courts (FTC) to ensure expeditious trials in paper leak cases in the wake of the 2026 NEET fiasco, the country’s Fast-Track Special Courts (FTSCs) — operating under the most recent scheme introduced in Oct 2019 — are buckling under mounting backlogs.Govt data analysed by TOI shows that annual disposals by FTSCs, created to deliver swift justice in some of the most sensitive criminal cases (rape and Pocso), dropped to 66,500 cases in 2025, down from a record 85,595 in 2024, a decline of more than 22%. At the same time, pending cases rose from a little more than 2 lakh at the end of 2024 to nearly 2.5 lakh by the close of 2025.The trend suggests that despite expanding judicial capacity, fresh cases continue to outnumber disposals. Since 2021, pendency has increased by nearly one-third, from around 1.8 lakh to nearly 2.5 lakh , even as annual disposals almost doubled between 2021 and 2024 before falling last year.The figures point to a structural challenge rather than a temporary slowdown. Fast-track courts were conceived to shorten the time victims wait for justice, but rising case inflows, judicial vacancies, infrastructure constraints and limited courtroom capacity have continued to push pendency upwards.The result is that courts designed to accelerate trials are themselves carrying growing backlogs.As per the latest information from the govt, the FTSC scheme currently operates 775 courts, including 398 exclusive POCSO courts, across the country. This is against a target of at least 790 courts that should have been functional. The courts have disposed of nearly 3.9 lakh cases since inception. Yet with nearly 2.5 lakh cases still pending, the gains have not translated into a sustained reduction in backlog.The experience varies widely across States. While some States have managed comparatively low pendency per court, others continue to operate under far heavier workloads, indicating that the effectiveness of the scheme depends not only on the number of courts but also on staffing, infrastructure and the volume of new cases entering the system.The latest figures relate specifically to Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs), which are a separate scheme launched by the Centre in Oct 2019 to hear rape and Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act cases, which has since been extended up to Sept 30, 2026. These should not be confused with the original Fast Track Courts (FTCs), which were introduced nearly two decades earlier — 880 of which are functional currently.These courts had disposed of more than 13 lakh cases in 2025, up from 11.7 lakh in 2024, but lower than 15.2 lakh in 2023. However, year-wise pendency data on FTCs wasn’t immediately available. The department of justice’s dashboard, which was accessible as of July 23 night, was offline on Friday.History Of Fast-Track CourtsIndia’s first FTCs were established in 2000 following the recommendations of the 11th Finance Commission. The idea was to create additional courts on a temporary basis to clear long-pending sessions cases and reduce the number of undertrial prisoners.The Centre funded the scheme until March 31, 2011, after which States were expected to use their own resources. While several States retained or expanded FTCs, others allowed them to lapse, leading to wide variations across the country.The policy then evolved after the 2012 Nirbhaya case, as public pressure mounted for quicker trials in sexual offence cases. The 14th Finance Commission later supported the creation of 1,800 Fast Track Courts using the increased fiscal space available to States, though without dedicated central funding.And, in Oct 2019 the FTSCs scheme under the Nirbhaya Fund was launched. Since then, the ordinary FTCs remain the responsibility of state govts and high courts, while the Centre funds only the FTSC scheme.
Article Summary: Fast-track courts were conceived to shorten the time victims wait for justice. Rising case inflows, judicial vacancies, infrastructure constraints and limited courtroom capacity have continued to push pendency upwards. The result is that courts designed to accelerate trials are themselves carrying growing backlogs.

Article Title: Indian seafarer killed after ship attacked in Black Sea; MEA condemns incident
Article Text:
Indian seafarer killed after ship attacked in Black Sea; MEA condemns incident

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Friday condemned the attack on the commercial vessel MV OMORFI in the Black Sea that killed an Indian national, calling attacks on commercial shipping 'unacceptable' and urging all parties to ensure the safety of maritime navigation and global trade.The incident took place on July 18, when the MV OMORFI was attacked while transiting the Black Sea, reportedly in Russian territorial waters. According to the MEA, there were 10 crew members on board, including three Indian nationals. One Indian citizen was killed in the attack, while the other two Indians are reported to be safe.In a statement, the MEA said, "On 18 July 2026, the commercial vessel MV OMORFI was attacked while transiting the Black Sea, reportedly in Russian territorial waters. At the time of the incident, there were ten crew members on board, including three Indian nationals. As per available information, one Indian national tragically lost his life in the attack. We extend our deepest condolences to the bereaved family of the deceased. The other two Indian nationals on board are reported to be safe."Condemning the attack, the ministry said, "India unequivocally condemns such attacks targeting commercial shipping and placing the lives of innocent civilian crew members at risk.It is a matter of serious concern that the freedom of navigation and international commerce is facing increasing threats. India calls upon all concerned parties to uphold international obligations to ensure the safety and security of maritime navigation and uninterrupted flow of global commerce. "The latest attack comes after MV Golden Leo, a Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo vessel, was struck shortly after departing Ukraine's port of Odesa on July 19. The vessel had 17 crew members, including five Indian nationals. Four Indians were killed and one was critically injured in that attack.The MEA had then condemned the strike, saying commercial shipping and civilian crew members should not be targeted, while assuring that India's mission in Ukraine was extending all possible assistance to those affected.The back-to-back attacks have heightened concerns over the safety of commercial shipping in the Black Sea, where renewed hostilities have increased risks to civilian vessels and global maritime trade.
Article Summary: The incident took place on July 18, when the MV OMORFI was attacked. According to the MEA, there were 10 crew members on board, including three Indian nationals. One Indian citizen was killed in the attack, while the other two Indians are reported to be safe.

Article Title: Three chemical parks to be set up under BHAVYA-Rasayan scheme
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Union Cabinet on Friday approved the Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana Rasayan (BHAVYA-Rasayan) scheme for establishing three dedicated chemical parks in the country.The scheme will have a total financial outlay of Rs 3,030 crore, of which Rs 3,000 crore will be used for establishing common infrastructure facilities and basic utilities inside the parks, while the remaining Rs 30 crore has been earmarked for administrative expenditure.Announced in the Union Budget, the scheme will run for five years. While the Centre will provide a grant of up to Rs 1,000 crore for each park, the state where it is established will have to contribute at least Rs 500 crore.Govt said the BHAVYA-Rasayan scheme is expected to promote the development of the chemical industry and its value chain, including upstream, downstream and ancillary industries, while ensuring efficient utilisation of resources.By providing shared common infrastructure facilities and basic utilities tailored to the needs of the chemical industry, the scheme is expected to enhance cost competitiveness and make the Indian chemical industry globally competitive. It will also help the sector integrate better with global value chains, boosting exports and import substitution.The scheme will create an environment-friendly ecosystem with centralised facilities such as a common effluent treatment plant, treatment, storage and disposal facilities, and hazardous waste management infrastructure. Govt said the development of the chemical sector will generate employment and contribute to economic growth.
Article Summary: The scheme will have a total financial outlay of Rs 3,030 crore. The Centre will provide a grant of up to Rs 1,000 crore for each park. The state where it is established will have to contribute at least Rs 500 crore.

Article Title: Government pushes competition in power distribution
Article Text:
.

NEW DELHI: Union power ministry’s consultative committee met on Thursday to discuss a consumer-centric framework for parallel distribution licensing that would allow multiple electricity suppliers to use the same distribution network.The proposed reform aims to improve service quality, encourage competition, reduce infrastructure duplication and give consumers the freedom to choose their electricity provider.The draft National Electricity Policy-2026, which is under consultation and is likely to be placed before the cabinet soon, has also underlined the need to phase out monopoly in electricity distribution and introduce competition by allowing multiple players.According to officials, the existing legal framework permits more than one distribution licensee in the same area, but requires each of them to establish its own distribution network. This results in duplication of infrastructure, higher capital expenditure, discourages fresh investment and leads to “inefficient utilisation of resources”.Mumbai is the only city where consumers have exercised supplier choice for several years, while the distribution network is developed in a coordinated manner under the supervision of the state electricity regulatory commission.Emphasising the consumer-centric nature of the reform, Union power minister Manohar Lal said consumers would have the freedom to choose their electricity supplier, similar to the choices available today in sectors such as telecom and aviation. "Increased competition is expected to encourage better consumer service, improved reliability, greater innovation and operational efficiency, while ensuring optimal utilisation of existing infrastructure and avoiding unnecessary expenditure," the minister said at the meeting.Power ministry, in a statement, said members of Parliament who are part of the consultative committee offered valuable suggestions on the proposed framework. Under the proposal, existing distribution licensees will continue to own, operate and maintain their networks."New distribution licensees will be able to use the existing network by paying regulated wheeling charges, while retaining the option to develop their own network wherever permitted by the concerned state electricity regulatory commission," govt said in the statement.
Article Summary: Proposed reform aims to improve service quality, encourage competition, reduce infrastructure duplication and give consumers the freedom to choose their electricity provider. Draft National Electricity Policy-2026 is under consultation and is likely to be placed before the cabinet soon. Under the proposal, existing distribution licensees will continue to own, operate and maintain their networks.

Article Title: NTA terminates 47 officials, begins specialist-led rebuild
Article Text:
.

NEW DELHI: The National Testing Agency has terminated 47 officials and begun rebuilding its workforce with specialist leadership in cybersecurity, forensic investigation, test-centre operations and assessment research, government sources said on Friday.Some of those terminated will also face legal and criminal action based on internal inquiries and inputs from investigating agencies. More measures are expected as responsibility is fixed for failures in national entrance examinations.The first phase includes four General Manager appointments and 16 Young Professionals through UPSC’s PRATIBHA Setu portal. Recruitment will be overseen by the K Radhakrishnan-led monitoring committee, which will hold its first meeting on Saturday, July 25, ministry sources said.The crackdown follows the NEET-UG paper leak, which forced nearly 20 lakh candidates to take the examination again on June 21 after the May 3 test was cancelled. Sources stressed that the 47 personnel had been terminated, not merely transferred or marked for removal. Their names, ranks and alleged roles were not disclosed. Cases indicating criminal wrongdoing will be referred to the appropriate agencies, while departmental and legal proceedings will follow separately.The four General Managers will be appointed on three-year contracts.The assessment and psychometrics head will oversee question banks, normalisation, equating and calibration, and pilots on computer-adaptive testing and AI-assisted assessment.The test-centre operations head will supervise NTA ’s network across more than 500 cities and select overseas centres, including empanelment, capacity, accessibility, amenities, examination-day operations and coordination with administrations.The information-security head will serve as Chief Information Security Officer, responsible for systems, networks, applications, candidate data, a round-the-clock Security Operations Centre and compliance with data-protection, information-technology and CERT-In requirements.The vigilance, investigation and forensics head will lead malpractice inquiries, build in-house digital-forensics capability and coordinate with the CBI, Intelligence Bureau, Enforcement Directorate, state police and cybercrime units under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.NTA will also engage 16 Young Professionals through PRATIBHA Setu — Professional Resource And Talent Integration Bridge for Hiring Aspirants — for the first time. The platform gives verified employers access to willing candidates who cleared stages of UPSC examinations but were not recommended in the final merit list.Twelve positions will be in academic research, two in legal research and two in finance and accounts. Appointments will initially be for 24 months, extendable to 36 months based on performance.The changes seek to reduce NTA’s dependence on temporary manpower. It has 39 sanctioned permanent posts, all on deputation, but only 24 are filled, against 73 contractual personnel and 124 outsourced workers.Further hiring will follow across 10 functional verticals recommended by the Radhakrishnan committee. NTA has also initiated fresh empanelment of subject experts and translators.The overhaul will accompany changes to examination delivery. NEET-UG will shift from OMR-based testing to computer-based testing from 2027, bringing it closer to JEE Main and CUET. The move should reduce physical movement of papers, enable multiple question sets and create a digital trail, but will require secure centres, stronger cybersecurity and safeguards against technical failures.The government is also reviewing outsourcing in registration, centre management, technology services and handling of confidential material. The new model will define responsibility, strengthen audits and background checks, reduce agencies handling sensitive information and impose tougher penalties for security failures.Sources said the reset would combine accountability for past lapses with safeguards against future leaks and malpractice.
Article Summary: The first phase includes four General Manager appointments and 16 Young Professionals through UPSC’s PRATIBHA Setu portal. Recruitment will be overseen by the K Radhakrishnan-led monitoring committee, which will hold its first meeting on Saturday, July 25.

Article Title: PM Modi gains 1 million Instagram followers overnight after selfie video amid NEET protest
Article Text:
PM Modi gains 1 million Instagram followers overnight after selfie video

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi gained around 1 million Instagram followers overnight after he released his selfie video on Thursday night addressing concerns of the NEET paper leak.Currently PM Modi has 102 million followers on Instagram. His video captioned: "More strict actions against paper leaks to come in tomorrow’s Cabinet!" has garnered 271 million views so far along with 15 million likes and 1.3 million comments on Instagram.In the video, he announced that the government would introduce tougher measures to tackle examination paper leaks. He also informed about the Union Cabinet meeting agenda held on Friday."I know that paper leak is not an ordinary issue. It is very painful for lakh of students and their guardians," he said."Numerous effective measures have been taken in the past two and a half months since the paper leak incident. The culprits have been caught and are in jail. Our most important responsibility was to ensure that students' year is not wasted. The government used all its might to ensure that 22 lakh students could take their exams in the shortest possible time," he added.The Union Cabinet on Friday cleared amendments to the anti-paper leak law, proposing stricter punishment for those involved in examination paper leaks. Sources said the revised law prescribes up to 10 years in prison and a fine of as much as Rs 10 crore, while raising the minimum jail term from three years to five years.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi gains 1 million Instagram followers overnight after selfie video. His video captioned: "More strict actions against paper leaks to come in tomorrow’s Cabinet!" has garnered 271 million views so far along with 15 million likes and 1.3 million comments on Instagram.

Article Title: 'There are Chinese projects on territories in J&K that belong to India': MEA objects to illegal occupation
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Ministry of external affairs on Friday accused China of violating India's sovereignty and said that it is "illegally occupying" Indian territories in Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh.During a weekly press briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that the government objects to the Chinese projects in Jammu and Kashmir."EAM said that when it comes to sovereignty issues, it is actually India that should be and is raising them. India does not violate China’s sovereignty in any manner and has been consistent," Jaiswal said."But China has been in illegal occupation of Indian territories in Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh since 1963, where India’s right is officially acknowledged even by China. There are Chinese projects on territories in Jammu and Kashmir that belong to India, and we object to that," he added.This comes a day after external affairs minister S Jaishankar met his Chinese counterpart Wang Yi on the sidelines of Asean summit in Manila,According to the Chinese foreign ministry readout, Wang said the meetings between Chinese President Xi Jinping and Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Kazan and Tianjin had "guided China-India relations onto the right track of improvement and development.""China and India are partners, not competitors, and opportunities, not threats, for each other," Wang said, adding that institutional exchanges between the two countries had gradually resumed, border areas had maintained peace and tranquillity, and bilateral trade had reached a new high."These achievements have not come easily and should be cherished," he said.Calling China and India representatives of emerging economies and key members of the Global South, Wang said the two countries should "prioritise human well-being, demonstrate their responsibility as major powers, consolidate the positive momentum of bilateral relations, strengthen coordination and cooperation in international and regional affairs, and make positive contributions to promoting multipolarity and the democratisation of international relations. "He said China was willing to work with India to implement the consensus reached by the two leaders, maintain close high-level exchanges, expand cooperation in trade, media and people-to-people exchanges, properly handle sensitive issues, and "explore a correct way for neighbouring major powers to coexist peacefully, based on mutual respect, mutual trust, common development, and common prosperity.
Article Summary: MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that the government objects to the Chinese projects in Jammu and Kashmir. This comes a day after external affairs minister S Jaishankar met his Chinese counterpart Wang Yi. Wang said the meetings between Chinese President Xi Jinping and Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Kazan and Tianjin had "guided China-India relations onto the right track of improvement and development"

Article Title: Up to 10-year jail & Rs 10 crore fine: Cabinet clears tougher anti-paper leak bill
Article Text:
The Union Cabinet on Friday approved amendments to the anti-paper leak law, proposing up to 10 years' imprisonment and a fine of up to Rs 10 crore for offenders.

Government to introduce Bill in Parliament soon

Rijiju criticises Opposition over Parliament disruptions

Cabinet decision comes amid talks with protesting students

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you support the proposed amendments to the Prevention of Paper Leak law? Yes, tougher penalties are necessary. No, the current penalties are sufficient. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Union cabinet on Friday approved amendments to the Prevention of Paper Leak law, proposing tougher penalties for those involved in examination paper leaks.According to sources, the proposed legislation provides for a maximum jail term of 10 years and a fine of up to Rs 10 crore.It also seeks to increase the minimum imprisonment for individuals convicted in paper leak cases from the current three years to five years.The move comes amid nationwide protests over alleged irregularities in the NEET examination and growing demands for stricter safeguards to protect the integrity of competitive exams.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the government would soon introduce the legislation in Parliament, adding that the PM Modi had directed that there should be no delay in bringing the Bill."We are preparing to present the bill, but after you receive the briefing on our cabinet decision, we will inform you about our timing. The Prime Minister has said that there should be no delay in the bill we are bringing regarding students. The country also wants what the Prime Minister has said, so it would not be right to resort to any tactics to obstruct it... Congress will fall into this if they continue to disrupt the parliamentary proceedings.We are taking important steps for the future of the students. If the Congress party continues to create all kinds of hurdles to prevent parliamentary discussion, then they will have to face the brunt of the youth of this nation and, in fact, the entire nation," Rijiju said.Rijiju accused the Opposition of preventing a discussion on the NEET paper leak issue in Parliament, saying the government had repeatedly sought a debate."For 5 days, we were unable to discuss the NEET paper leak. So, we appealed today as well. Our minister will brief us on the important cabinet decision. Rahul Gandhi was in the House today, so we asked that the debate begin immediately. Now, the Congress party has shown that it's not interested in debate. Those who were protesting, and Sonam Wangchuk, the most prominent figure among the protesters, also broke his hunger strike and said that the discussion should take place now. I don't think there's any benefit in politicising this. We should focus on how to take concrete steps and the future of the students," he said.The minister appealed to the Opposition to allow Parliament to function, saying the focus should remain on strengthening the examination system."The future of the students and how we can ensure a proper and very strong system in place for the future of the students; this has to be our priority. By disrupting the parliamentary procedures and the House, it will not yield any result. I would like to request once again of Rahul Gandhi and all the opposition members that better sense should prevail. You cannot indefinitely create trouble in the Parliament to prevent discussion. It is wasting the time of all of the members... It is very critical to let the Parliament function, and when all matters are to be discussed. Taking to the demands of all the members: Why the Congress Party and some of their allies are disturbing the parliamentary proceedings. I do not understand. It would be nice if they could make any demands. But they can make it during their intervention," Rijiju said.The Cabinet's decision comes a day after Union ministers held talks with representatives of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), which has been leading protests over the NEET paper leak controversy.Following the meeting, CJP leaders said the government had sought time till Saturday afternoon to decide on their demand for Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. They also claimed the Centre had given in-principle approval to two other demands, including compensation for the families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide and withdrawal of FIRs and legal cases against protesting students.The government initiated the dialogue after social activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike following written assurances from the Centre on reforms to the competitive examination system. Ahead of the Cabinet meeting, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had announced that the government would consider a draft Bill providing for fast-track courts and stricter punishment for paper leak offenders, saying, "More strict actions against paper leaks to come in tomorrow's Cabinet!"
Article Summary: The Union Cabinet on Friday approved amendments to the Prevention of Paper Leak law. The proposed legislation provides for a maximum jail term of 10 years and a fine of up to Rs 10 crore. The move comes amid nationwide protests over alleged irregularities in the NEET examination and growing demands for stricter safeguards.

Article Title: Jantar Mantar clash: Supreme Court to hear pleas on alleged police excesses on July 27
Article Text:
Jantar Mantar clash: Supreme Court to hear pleas on alleged police excesses on July 27

(with inputs from agency)

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday agreed to hear on July 27 two petitions alleging excessive police action against students who participated in protests over the alleged NEET paper leak at Delhi's Jantar Mantar and other parts of the country.The matter was mentioned before a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana. Senior advocates Shyam Divan and Gopal Sankaranarayanan requested an early hearing, informing the court that the petitions had been filed and numbered by the Supreme Court registry.The protests were held in several states following allegations of irregularities in the NEET examination. In Delhi, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led march on July 20 witnessed clashes between protesters and security personnel, who used lathis and tear gas to disperse crowds attempting to march towards Parliament. The protesters were demanding the resignation of union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged paper leak.Separately, while hearing a batch of petitions related to the NEET paper leak, another Supreme Court bench said it would closely monitor the Centre's efforts to prevent future examination leaks and stressed the need for long-term reforms.A bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe asked the Centre to explain the steps taken to improve transparency, implement the recommendations of the Radhakrishnan Committee, and adopt the proposed IIT model for conducting examinations.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre, told the court that the government would file a detailed report outlining measures that go beyond the committee's recommendations."Students' futures can't be jeopardised. We are going beyond the Radhakrishnan Committee. I assure you that the government is walking 10 extra miles. I can assure you everything is being supervised at the highest level," Mehta said.The bench observed that while the Air Force had been used to transport question papers for the NEET-UG re-test, such measures were temporary."Ad hocism has troubled us for years," Justice Narasimha observed, adding that the court would ensure the examination process is institutionalised.During the hearing, advocate Tanvi Dubey, appearing for the Federation of All India Medical Association (FAIMA), sought a detailed standard operating procedure for the computer-based testing model that the National Testing Agency plans to implement for NEET-UG from next year.
Article Summary: Supreme Court to hear two petitions alleging excessive police action against students in NEET protests. The protests were held in several states following allegations of irregularities in the NEET examination. Protesters were demanding the resignation of union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged paper leak.

Article Title: 'Substantial risk of misuse by anti-national elements': Government directs GitHub to take down Bluetooth-based Bitchat app
Article Text:
The app allows anonymous communication without mandatory user registration, phone number verification or centralised logging of messages

Govt flags anonymous, offline messaging as security risk

Notice follows use of offline messaging apps during Delhi protests

NEW DELHI: The Union government's cybercrime coordination centre has directed Microsoft-owned GitHub to remove Bitchat, a Bluetooth-based messaging application developed by former Twitter CEO Jack Dorsey, citing concerns that it could be misused by terrorists, organised crime groups and anti-national elements to evade lawful surveillance.The notice comes after authorities observed several participants in the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar using Bluetooth-based messaging applications after temporary internet restrictions were imposed around the protest site.Sharing a copy of the July 23 notice on X on Friday, Dorsey claimed, "The Government of India does not like technologies like Bitchat and wants it taken down."The Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C), which functions under the Union home ministry, has not immediately responded to queries regarding the notice, according to news agency PTI.In its notice to GitHub, I4C said Bitchat is among a number of applications capable of enabling decentralised peer-to-peer messaging over Bluetooth mesh networks without relying on mobile networks, internet connectivity or centralised servers.According to the notice, the application allows anonymous communication without mandatory user registration, phone number verification or centralised logging of messages."The technical architecture of the application significantly impedes lawful interception, attribution and investigation by law enforcement agencies," the notice said.The agency argued that because messages are transmitted directly between nearby devices through a decentralised mesh network, such platforms could be used to evade lawful surveillance, facilitate anonymous coordination and bypass internet restrictions imposed during situations involving public disorder, riots, terrorism, organised crime or internet shutdowns."Intelligence inputs indicate that such decentralised communication platforms are capable of being exploited for coordinating unlawful assemblies, violent protests, dissemination of misinformation, radicalisation, criminal conspiracies, and other activities prejudicial to the sovereignty and integrity of India, defence of India, security of the State, public order, and for facilitating the commission of cognizable offences," the notice stated.It further said the absence of a centralised service provider limits the ability of law enforcement agencies to obtain subscriber information, communication records or timely assistance during investigations."The application's design, which enables communication even during network restrictions, creates a substantial risk of misuse by anti-national elements, terrorist organisations, organised criminal groups, and cybercriminals seeking to evade lawful detection and continue communication despite legally imposed restrictions," the notice added.I4C has alleged that the app violates Sections 43, 84B and 84C of the Information Technology Act, along with Section 61 read with Sections 196 and 197 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.The CJP has been leading protests over the NEET paper leak and is demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.Earlier on Friday, representatives of the CJP held a nearly two-hour meeting with Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh.Following the meeting, the outfit reiterated that Pradhan's resignation remained a "non-negotiable" demand and also sought Rs 1 crore compensation for families of students who died by suicide after the cancellation of the NEET examination, along with the withdrawal of FIRs against protesters.Union health minister JP Nadda said the CJP delegation had presented three key demands and five suggestions for examination reforms, and the government would respond after internal discussions.Another round of talks between the two sides is scheduled for Saturday.
Article Summary: Bitchat allows anonymous communication without mandatory user registration, phone number verification or centralised logging of messages. Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C), which functions under the Union home ministry, has not immediately responded to queries regarding the notice. I4C has alleged that the app violates Sections 43, 84B and 84C of the Information Technology Act.

Article Title: 2 new secretaries in education ministry, Vineet Joshi moved to panchayati raj
Article Text:
Joshi moved to panchayati raj

NEW DELHI: Amid ongoing protests over NEET-UG paper leak issue, govt Thursday named new secretaries for higher and school education departments, with incumbent Vineet Joshi, who had charge of both, moved to low-profile panchayati raj department.While animal husbandry secretary Naresh Pal Gangwar was appointed the new secretary for higher education, TK Anil Kumar will be the new school education secretary. The changes mark an overhaul of sorts in education ministry bureaucracy, as Abhishek Singh was earlier named head of the National Testing Agency , which conducts NEET, CUET and other exams.In early June, CBSE chief Rahul Singh and secretary Himanshu Gupta were transferred out of the National Testing Agency after a controversy over on-screen marking.The secretary-level appointments included 13 new department heads, including a bifurcation of ministry of housing and urban affairs. MoHUA secretary K Srinivas has been shifted to development of north eastern region (DoNER) ministry. D Thara, from Gujarat cadre, has been appointed secretary of the just-created department of capital development, while her batchmate Satendra Singh from Jharkhand will lead the department of urban development.The changes in education ministry are significant as govt has said demand for removal of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan is not under consideration, but steps will be taken to address concerns. The appointments committee of cabinet also desginated Chandra Bhushan Kumar as new labour secretary, while Keshav Chandra will be the new mines secretary. Odisha cadre IAS officer SK Lohani has been designated as animal husbandry secretary.
Article Summary: Vineet Joshi, who had charge of both, moved to low-profile panchayati raj department. The changes mark an overhaul of sorts in education ministry bureaucracy. Abhishek Singh was earlier named head of the National Testing Agency.

Article Title: 'Paper leaks are no ordinary matter': What PM Modi said in his midnight video message
Article Text:
PM Modi promises tougher action in midnight address
